findings.text: The new KeyError-to-BindingTransformError conversion in _NetCDFStoreArrays.read is correctly scoped to binding.struct_array_entry is not None, so an empty first struct array under a selecting binding now names the binding as the run claims. A NON-selecting binding over an empty struct array still surfaces a bare KeyError, raised by _struct_array_positions (line 191) before the read's rank check, or by _read_ids_path (line 262) for a later empty array. This is pre-existing behaviour, outside this node's stated goal (the selecting-binding rank), and unreachable for the JT-60SA store whose coils are non-empty; recorded as a follow-on rather than a defect of this change.

follow_ons: Resolves the prior node's review finding 2 (r-20261006T025925726270-review-of-jtmm-static-entry-selector): a selecting binding over an empty first struct array no longer raises a bare KeyError but a BindingTransformError naming the binding, covered by test_selecting_binding_over_an_empty_struct_array_is_refused.

Resolves the prior node's review finding 1: the new test_selecting_binding_counts_only_levels_below_the_consumed_struct_array exercises struct_array_entry together with a preserved position below the selected level (source_rank 1 preserves the element level, shape (1,), beneath the consumed coil level), the selector-plus-preserved-position composition the plan asserts and the earlier node left untested.
The non-selecting empty-struct-array KeyError noted in the finding is a separate concern for whichever node next touches the empty-array error family.

item_verdicts.call_sites: _NetCDFStoreArrays.read, _struct_array_positions and _read_ids_path have no callers outside transform_engine.py; the change alters only the internal read path and the existing BindingsTransformError/TransformEngineError family (BindingTransformError subclasses TransformEngineError, line 43). No new public symbol, no signature change, and no machine-name branch is introduced.
item_verdicts.diff: The fix in read() adds: a try/except around _struct_array_positions converting its empty-struct-array KeyError to a BindingTransformError naming the binding when a selector is declared; consumed_levels = 1 for a selecting binding and 0 otherwise; the rank bound available_levels = len(positions) - consumed_levels; and the preserved slice positions[consumed_levels:][-structural_rank:]. For a binding without the slot consumed_levels is 0, so available_levels, the rank bound and the preserved slice are byte-for-byte the pre-fix expression -- existing bindings are unaffected, as claimed and as the unchanged base-arm-passing bindings attest.

item_verdicts.goal: The plan (imas-ambix:jt60sa-machine-map section 4) states the selector 'consumes the first struct-array level: the named entry is read and that level contributes no axis. source_rank then counts the leaf and the struct levels below it'. The node delivers exactly this: _NetCDFStoreArrays.read computes consumed_levels = 1 when struct_array_entry is set, bounds the rank check by available_levels = len(positions) - consumed_levels, and preserves only positions[consumed_levels:]. Selecting coil C reads shape (1,) at source_rank 1 (the element level preserved), a scalar at 0, and source_rank 2 (which would count the consumed coil level) is refused under BindingTransformError naming the binding and the rank -- all independently reproduced off an unmutated export of the reviewed head.

justifications: Independent review of run r-20261006T031703442015-jtmm-selector-rank-composition (plan imas-ambix:jt60sa-machine-map section 4), reviewed_base_sha 0a2735d1fd58862bda44f060f8e8c73baef20e5b, reviewed_head_sha 6172d7519c67df08bf8b9de444c30ab0dc500934, stored as a parsed record scoring all six dimensions in 0..20 -- goal_fidelity 20, evidence 19, scope_discipline 20, durability 19, fit 20, reuse 20 -- total 118/120, added_failure_count 0 with added_failure_ids []. Goal fidelity is full: the node implements the plan section 4 sentence verbatim, correcting the prior node's rank check symmetry by making the consumed struct-array level contribute no axis, and I reproduced both the raised defect (source_rank 2 silently yielded shape (1,) pre-fix) and the refusal at head off an unmutated export of the reviewed commit. Scope is clean -- three declared files, no catalogue or data artefact touched, single commit, worktree clean. Fit and reuse are strong: the change extends the existing read path and error family with a two-line adjustment and a scoped exception conversion, leaving non-selecting bindings byte-for-byte unchanged and adding no parallel path or machine-name branch. Durability is high and deliberately not full: two new tests guard the fixed behaviour including the selector-plus-preserved-position composition the earlier node left untested, and the declared negative control reproduces, but the re-slice observations: the empty-array conversion covers only the selecting case (a non-selecting empty array still raises a bare KeyError, recorded as a follow-on, pre-existing and out of scope). Evidence is strong (both arms green and consistent with their logs, negative control reproduced) but rests on a single small synthetic store rather than the real JT-60SA netCDF, so it scores one below the maximum. This run closes both findings the prior node's review recorded; no regression and no defect of this change found.
